previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("I don't want to read an old inbox") The inbox now shows ports only for live sessions, meaning each agent's current session in the Agency registry, and only ones opened from today on. That's 184 ports in 13 sessions instead of 2,827. Older ports are still in the store, where queries can reach them.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("if orphaned items raise a warning in the future") When an agent's registry session changes and your asks are still open in the session it left, the fault intake raises one warning for that session, listing the asks. If that session's replies had no marks, the warning is low severity and says "answered or not is unknown", since nothing can tell. Agents' own offers lapse silently. The first pass only records who is live, so no history gets reported. Tests cover the change case, the unchanged case, the unmarked case and the old-ask cutoff.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("feed them into report-futon-bug") `fault_intake.py report <fault-id>` writes a normal report-futon-bug report with the stranded asks inline, under `~/notes/futon-bugs/`, ready to read or bell. It works for any fault, not just orphans.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (my breakage) While restarting the jobs, I accidentally killed the scratch store on :7093. `bg.py list` prints several jobs per line, and my grep picked up the store's id along with the follower's. It was down for about 3 minutes. I restarted it, its data was intact, and the writers caught up on their next passes. I've saved a memory note: kill jobs only by their exact id.
